AR-2026F-SB7.aiSummary: The bill would set spending limits for the Arkansas Department of Commerce’s State Insurance Department for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers money for staff pay, office costs, fraud investigations, funeral services, prepaid funeral benefits, refunds of overpayments, continuing education, and health information counseling. The bill also sets the highest number of regular and temporary workers allowed for the department.

AR-2026F-SB10.aiSummary: The measure sets state spending for the Arkansas Department of Commerce, Division of Workforce Services, for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers salaries, office costs, unemployment benefit payments, training help, grants, and other work of the division. The bill includes several funding pots, including $16,258,332 for operations, $63,610,021 from the trust fund, and $702,000,001 for unemployment benefits and related expenses.

AR-2026F-HR1052.aiSummary: This resolution would take away Arkansas Girls State’s access to the House chamber for its 2026 meeting and would bar it from using bill drafting help from the Bureau of Legislative Research. If the Speaker later decides the students who were denied a chance to participate have been allowed to join the 2026 meeting, the change would be undone and the access restored. It also urges the American Legion Auxiliary to reconsider any decision that would block those students from taking part.

AR-2026F-HR1016.aiSummary: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to create a state law about certain residential property deals owned by business entities. The bill would require clear disclosure that a buyer is buying an interest in the entity, not the home itself, and it would limit certain rules on transfers, fees, and dispute forums. It would also give the Attorney General enforcement power and set some exceptions for certain religious and nonprofit property and for time-share interests.
